name.text: Estimate the gradient of a tangent by drawing it (INNODEMS)

questiontext.text:
The graph shows \( f(x) = {@fdisp@} \). The point \(P\) lies on the curve at \( x = {@x0@} \), so \( P = ({@x0@},\ {@y0@}) \).

Drag the point \(Q\) so that the line through \(P\) and \(Q\) is the tangent to the curve at \(P\) — the straight line that just kisses the curve there. The dashed triangle shows the run and rise between \(P\) and \(Q\); the box shows their coordinates.

[[jsxgraph input-ref-ans1="ref_Q" width='540px' height='460px']] JXG.Options.text.useMathJax = true; var aa = {#aa#}, x0 = {#x0#}, y0 = {#y0#}; var xmax = {#float(xmax)#}, ymax = {#float(ymax)#}; var Qx = {#float(qix)#}, Qy = {#float(qiy)#}; var f = function (x) { return aa * Math.sqrt(x); }; var board = JXG.JSXGraph.initBoard(divid, { boundingbox: [-1, ymax, xmax, -1], keepaspectratio: true, axis: true, grid: {majorStep: 1, minorStep: 0.5}, showCopyright: false, pan: {enabled: false}, }); // The curve f(x) = a*sqrt(x). Draw from x = 0 (its domain start) to the LIVE right // edge of the board, so it spans the full visible width even though keepaspectratio // makes the visible x-range wider than xmax. board.create('functiongraph', [f, 0, function () { return board.getBoundingBox()[2]; } ], {strokeColor: '#0055bb', strokeWidth: 2.5, name: ''}); board.create('text', [x0 - 0.2, y0 - 1.1, '\\(y = ' + (aa === 1 ? '' : aa) + '\\sqrt{x}\\)'], {color: '#0055bb', fontSize: 15, fixed: true}); // Fixed point P, given on the curve. var P = board.create('point', [x0, y0], {name: 'P', fixed: true, size: 4, strokeColor: '#c62828', fillColor: '#c62828', label: {offset: [-16, 8], color: '#c62828', fontSize: 15}}); // Free draggable point Q, snapped to the 0.5 grid so its coordinates are exact. var Q = board.create('point', [Qx, Qy], {name: 'Q', size: 5, strokeColor: '#1565c0', fillColor: '#1565c0', label: {offset: [10, 10], color: '#1565c0', fontSize: 15}}); // The student's line through P and Q (a full straight line). board.create('line', [P, Q], {strokeColor: '#2e7d32', strokeWidth: 2.5, straightFirst: true, straightLast: true}); // Rise/run triangle - drawn but deliberately NOT labelled with values. var corner = function () { return [Q.X(), P.Y()]; }; board.create('segment', [P, corner], {strokeColor: '#888', strokeWidth: 1.5, dash: 2}); board.create('segment', [corner, Q], {strokeColor: '#888', strokeWidth: 1.5, dash: 2}); // Readout: the coordinates of P and Q only (never the slope). Top-left, in the // empty region under the rising curve. board.create('text', [ function () { return board.getBoundingBox()[0] + 0.3; }, function () { return board.getBoundingBox()[1] - 0.3; }, function () { return '

[[input:ans1]]

[[validation:ans1]]

Now use the coordinates of \(P\) and \(Q\) to work out the gradient of the line you drew — your estimate of the derivative \( f'({@x0@}) \). Give your answer to 3 decimal places.

\( f'({@x0@}) \approx \) [[input:ans2]] [[validation:ans2]] [[feedback:prt2]]

generalfeedback.text:
The gradient of the tangent at a point is the derivative there. For \( f(x) = {@fdisp@} = {@aa@}x^{1/2} \), the rules in later sections give \( f'(x) = \dfrac{ {@aa@} }{2\sqrt{x}} \), so at \( x = {@x0@} \)

\[ f'({@x0@}) = \frac{ {@aa@} }{2\sqrt{ {@x0@} }} = {@m@} \approx {@md3@}. \]

To estimate this from the graph without the rule: draw the tangent at \(P\), pick a second point \(Q\) on it, and compute the gradient as

\[ \frac{\text{rise}}{\text{run}} = \frac{y_Q - y_P}{x_Q - x_P}. \]

Reading the coordinates to 3 decimal places makes this precise. A well-drawn tangent gives a gradient close to \( {@md3@} \).

The two marks are independent: one for drawing a good tangent (its slope close to the true value), and one for correctly computing the gradient of the line you actually drew. You can earn the computation mark even if your tangent is a little off — as long as your number matches your line.

node.description: Is the drawn line vertical (Q directly above/below P)?

truefeedback.text: Your line is vertical — \(Q\) is directly above \(P\), so the "run" is \(0\) and the gradient is undefined. Drag \(Q\) sideways so the line leans along the curve and just touches it at \(P\).

node.description: Is the drawn line's slope close to the true tangent slope?

truefeedback.text: Nicely done — your line just touches the curve at \(P\), so its slope is a good estimate of the tangent's gradient.

falsefeedback.text: Not a tangent yet. A tangent should just touch the curve at \(P\) and lean at the same steepness as the curve there — if it cuts across the curve or is too steep or too shallow, tilt \(Q\) until it grazes the curve at \(P\) only.

node.description: Does the stated gradient match the slope of the line the student drew?

truefeedback.text: Correct — that is exactly the gradient of the line you drew, computed as \(\dfrac{y_Q - y_P}{x_Q - x_P}\).

node.description: Did the student invert the ratio (run over rise)?

truefeedback.text: You've divided the wrong way round — that is the run over the rise, \(\dfrac{x_Q - x_P}{y_Q - y_P}\). Gradient is rise over run: \(\dfrac{y_Q - y_P}{x_Q - x_P}\). Turn your fraction the other way up.

falsefeedback.text: That doesn't match the line you drew. Read the coordinates of \(P\) and \(Q\) from the box, then compute \(\dfrac{y_Q - y_P}{x_Q - x_P}\) — the change in \(y\) divided by the change in \(x\) between the two points.

qtest.description: Correct: tangent drawn (Q on the tangent) and gradient computed correctly.
Process credit: tangent is off, but the gradient of the drawn line is computed correctly (prt2 still full).
Inverted computation: good tangent, but gradient given as run/rise.
Vertical line: Q directly above P (undefined slope); gradient stated wrongly.
